It runs in order n^2 time, but sorting really takes n log n time, so that is not good enough yet [2]. Insertion sort also gets a mention. It works in the reverse order from selection sort, and the instructor leaves it for you to work through at home [2]. The lecture then moves to merge sort [2].

So for the exam, the Lecture 3 progression is permutation sort, then selection sort, then insertion sort, then merge sort. For the lecture-by-lecture roadmap, check the Lecture 1 notes directly.
